move: dashboard cycles four colour themes via CSS variables, bars re-pop each switch
how: A mock analytics app (sidebar with four theme rows, stat tiles, a bar chart) is styled entirely from CSS custom properties on the stage. At 0.15, 0.4, 0.65 and 0.9 D a selection pill slides to the next theme row with expo.out, all eight custom properties tween to the new palette over 0.6s with power2.inOut (Daylight, Midnight, Lagoon, Ember, back to Daylight), a ring pulses out from the swatch, the theme label swaps with a small y fade and the bars and tile numbers re-enter with staggered expo.out. Between switches the bars breathe scaleY 0.85 to 1 with a slow sine yoyo so nothing is still.
adapt: Replace the four theme palettes and names, the brand name, tile numbers and bar heights with the product; the switch cadence of 1.5s per theme can stretch with D. Keep the 0.6s variable tween and the bar re-pop so each switch has a beat.
port: mount(el, shot) injects the app markup and sets the initial custom properties on el; animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with switches at 0.15 D + j*0.25 D, tweening the custom properties on el rather than .stage, and the label text set via a direction-safe onUpdate rather than the window.__fx.seek patch. Ring positions come from getBoundingClientRect so measure after mount.
caveats: .from(".tile b") lacks immediateRender:false, so the tile numbers most likely sit hidden until the first switch at 1.1s and the loop start does not match its end
the last switch bar and tile tweens run about 0.4s past D; boundary state is close but not identical
theme label text is corrected by patching window.__fx.seek
